name: Chapter 1: Electric Charges and Fields
description: Charge and its properties, Coulomb’s law, superposition, electric field and field lines, flux, dipoles, Gauss’s law and its applications

name: Chapter 2: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance
description: Potential and potential energy, dipole potential, equipotentials, E from V, conductors, dielectrics, capacitors, combinations, stored energy

name: Chapter 3: Current Electricity
description: Current, Ohm’s law, drift velocity, mobility, resistivity and temperature, power, emf and internal resistance, cells, Kirchhoff’s rules, Wheatstone bridge

name: Chapter 4: Moving Charges and Magnetism
description: Lorentz force, motion in B, Biot–Savart law, circular loop, Ampere’s law, solenoid, parallel currents, torque on a loop, galvanometer

name: Chapter 5: Magnetism and Matter
description: Bar magnet, field lines, dipole in B, Gauss’s law for magnetism, M, H, χ, dia-, para- and ferromagnetism

name: Chapter 6: Electromagnetic Induction
description: Faraday’s experiments, flux, Faraday’s and Lenz’s laws, motional emf, mutual and self inductance, magnetic energy, ac generator

name: Chapter 7: Alternating Current
description: rms values, phasors, R, L, C in ac, series LCR, resonance, power factor, transformers and power transmission

name: Chapter 8: Electromagnetic Waves
description: Displacement current, Maxwell’s equations, nature of EM waves, E₀ = cB₀, intensity, and the EM spectrum

name: Chapter 9: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments
description: Mirrors, refraction, total internal reflection, lenses, prisms, microscopes and telescopes with NEET/JEE-style problems

name: Chapter 10: Wave Optics
description: Huygens principle, interference, Young’s double slit, single-slit diffraction, polarisation and Malus’s law

name: Chapter 11: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
description: Electron emission, photoelectric effect, Einstein’s equation, photons, de Broglie waves and NEET/JEE-style problems
